summary.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore at a 7.99% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income reached INR115.44 crore, up 15.68% YoY, and EBITDA rose 36.24% to INR9.22 crore with margin up 121 bps to 7.99%. Net profit was INR6.40 crore (up 35% YoY, margin 5.54%), while EPS of INR3.23 grew only 3.53%. Management reiterated the INR500 crore FY27 revenue goal, flagged that the CCTV segment posted a Q1 loss due to project timing, and declined to commit to a margin expansion path beyond 1-2% over two years. Net debt, the share price fall since IPO, and buyback ideas drew pointed investor questions that management largely deflected toward growth investment.

segments.name: Security and manpower (standalone)
segments.commentary: Security revenue INR54.98 crore and housekeeping INR41.88 crore in June 2026 quarter; management cites ~9.95% EBITDA for manpower-type businesses (security, housekeeping, payroll).

segments.name: IFM and payroll
segments.commentary: IFM revenue INR10.28 crore and payroll services INR3.40 crore in the quarter; management says manpower businesses have similar profitability.

segments.name: CCTV and electronic security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2.11 crore with a loss at PAT level in Q1, attributed to project execution costs ahead of bill raising; management expects stabilisation by September quarter and calls it the most profitable segment. FY26 CCTV loss was about INR1.5 crore.

segments.name: Vocational training (LLP and Keertika Academy)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue nil (INR0 lakh); net loss about INR57 lakh across the LLP and Keertika Academy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target: cross INR500 crore consolidated, with management saying FY26 Nov-Dec onwards revenues will be booked for the full year, and expecting ~12-15% growth guidance to hold; management ambition of 20% growth stated but not committed.
FY27 EBITDA margin: management says Q1 is seasonally strongest, margins moderate in Q2-Q3 and recover in Q4; no firm FY27 margin expansion number given.
Medium term: Debajit Choudhury expects at least 1-2% EBITDA margin increase over the next two years, driven by electronics and mechanisation mix.
FY28 revenue: Kanad Mukherjee said FY28 will 'definitely cross INR600 crore', with range INR630-640 crore and a target of above INR650 crore by FY28.
CCTV/projects: targeted ~INR30 crore revenue this year (vs INR13-14 crore last year) and PAT of INR3.5-4 crore vs ~INR2.5 crore last year.
Debt: management says no increase in debt; debt levels to stay flat over FY27-FY28.
Free cash flow: average INR8-9 crore over the last 3-4 years; aim to lift to INR13-14 crore by moving systems revenue from INR13-14 crore to ~INR30 crore.
capex_capacity: DDU-GKY Odisha skill project awarded for INR7.93 crore; management expects ~INR4 crore billing this year; about six-month infrastructure gestation period and two-year contract tenor.

HDFC Bank command-and-control centre (CCTV-driven, subscription model, covering 100-150 branches): management expects INR1.5-2 crore investment (about INR1 crore for control room) and INR2-3 crore revenue; final stage negotiations.
Mumbai traffic and police projects: INR15-18 crore expected from one or two tenders; an INR2.18 crore Mumbai traffic tender already received.
NKDA AMC contract worth about INR6 crore expected, pending final tendering; SAIL Burnpur engagement targeted at INR4-5 crore this year.
Acquisitions: management says acquisitions are possible in the future for technology capabilities, but not immediate; no near-term plans for manpower-based acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Q1 order wins: 5 work orders from Reliance Projects and Property Management Services worth INR30.77 crore; 7 Reliance Group FM contracts worth INR14.94 crore (combined INR45.71 crore); 2 Nesco orders worth INR1.94 crore; West Bengal Public Department housekeeping order INR36.71 lakh.
Government GeM tenders now at around 3.85% (L1 pricing); management says it will be more selective in manpower GeM bids and focus on CCTV and DDU-GKY projects.
Customer mix: Reliance top client at INR46-47 crore annually; HDFC Bank ~INR18 crore; Anjali Jewellers ~INR12 crore; airports ~INR30 crore annually; Torrent Power ~INR6-7 crore.
Renewal rates ~96-97%; average client retention 4.5-5 years per management.
Geographic mix: West Bengal ~72-73% of revenue; growth push in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Bihar and Odisha.
Receivable cycle: bills raised after wages; client payment typically in about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Given 12-15% FY27 growth guidance, Q1 growth of ~16% and ~8% margin, is there scope to raise FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 revenues booked from Nov-Dec onwards will be booked for the full year in FY27, and it is confident of crossing INR500 crore this year. Q1 EBITDA is seasonally better, moderating in Q2-Q3 and recovering in Q4, so no margin expansion percentage was committed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 FY27 revenue split by segment and how has the mix changed?
qa_highlights.answer: June 2026 quarter: security INR54.98 crore, housekeeping INR41.88 crore, IFM INR10.28 crore, payroll INR3.40 crore (total INR110.53 crore); CCTV INR2.11 crore; small security and housekeeping INR1.29 crore; vocational training nil. Manpower EBITDA about 9.95%; CCTV PAT loss about INR1.27 lakh; vocational training net loss about INR57 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook and free cash flow target for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No increase in debt; debt levels to stay flat. Average FCF was INR8-9 crore over the last 3-4 years; aim to lift to INR13-14 crore by growing systems revenue from INR13-14 crore to about INR30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% growth an aspiration, and how will margins move from ~7% to 8-9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hope is to grow 20% without compromising the balance sheet, but no commitment. On margins, Kanad Mukherjee said expansion depends on project businesses catching up with manpower business; Debajit Choudhury expects at least 1-2% EBITDA margin increase over the next two years from electronics and mechanisation mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt, and why not a buyback given the share price fall since the IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone debt about INR69 crore vs cash about INR60 crore as of June; consolidated debt about INR82 crore. On the buyback proposal (13 lakh shares, about INR6 crore), Debajit Choudhury said the IPO capital is meant for growth, citing skill development capex, and did not commit to a buyback.

qa_highlights.question: Why was CCTV loss-making in Q1 and what is FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Project businesses incur Q1 losses due to execution spend before completion certificates and billing; FY26 CCTV loss was about INR1.5 crore. Management expects stabilisation by September quarter and targets about INR30 crore CCTV/projects revenue and PAT of INR3.5-4 crore this year. FY28: revenue to cross INR600 crore, range INR630-640 crore, target above INR650 crore.

risks_watch: Thin margin expansion visibility: management declined to give a firm FY27 margin number and expects Q2-Q3 moderation; medium-term 1-2% EBITDA uplift is the only figure given.
CCTV/projects execution: Q1 loss and reliance on lumpy tenders (Mumbai traffic INR15-18 crore, HDFC Bank command centre, NKDA AMC ~INR6 crore, SAIL INR4-5 crore) that are not yet awarded.
Pricing pressure in government manpower work: GeM L1 bids at about 3.85%, with management saying it will be more selective.
Working capital and receivables: about 3-month (90-day) client payment cycle; debt flat at about INR69 crore standalone and cash of INR60 crore as of June, with rising loans and advances.

Client concentration and renewal: Reliance at INR46-47 crore annually is the top client, and the DTET contract is under renewal with a loss already provided for; monitor renewal outcome and West Bengal concentration (72-73%).
Capital allocation and shareholder value: share price about INR46 vs IPO price INR111, buyback rejected in favour of growth capex; IPO funds unutilised INR36.85 crore as of June 2026.
key_quotes: So what we are seeing is that, last year we would have -- whatever revenues we had booked from November-December onwards that will get booked for the entire year during this financial year.
So whether there is going to be an expansion at the EBITDA margin at a percentage level is hard to say.
There will be no increase in debt. Debt levels will stay the same. There will be no increase in debt.
So I would expect at least an increase of about 1% to 2% in the EBITDA area over the next 2 years or so.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order inflows, growth and FY28 revenue targets, but cautious and evasive on margin expansion, buybacks and the share price decline, which management largely deflected toward growth investment. Several answers were qualified with "hard to say" or "let's see", and the CCTV loss was framed as seasonal timing.
